# silence-split

> Rust library that splits long PCM audio into pieces no longer than a maximum length, cutting in
> silence or at the quietest spot, with positions as sample indices in the original timeline.
> Version 0.1.0. Rust 1.85+. License MIT OR Apache-2.0.

## Pipeline

1. `Analyzer::new(Layout { sample_rate, channels }, &AnalyzeConfig::default())?`, then
   `push_interleaved(&[S])` or `push_planar(&[&[S]])` any number of times (`S` is `i16` or `f32`),
   then `finish() -> Analysis`. Alternatively
   `Analysis::from_scores(layout, len, score_rate, hop, scores) -> Result<Analysis, ConfigError>`.
2. `Analysis::segments(&SegmentConfig) -> Vec<Span>` and
   `Analysis::trim(&SegmentConfig) -> Option<Range<u64>>`. `Analysis::layout()` and
   `Analysis::sample_count()` return the original layout and length.
3. `plan(&Analysis, &SegmentConfig, &PlanConfig) -> Plan` or
   `adjust(&Analysis, &SegmentConfig, points: &[u64], window: Duration) -> Plan`.
4. Optionally `write_audacity_labels(&Plan, sample_rate, &mut impl core::fmt::Write)`.

## Positions and time

- Every public position is a `u64` sample index per channel in the original audio. Ranges are
  half-open `[start, end)`.
- Analysis frame `i` starts at original sample `floor(i * hop * sample_rate / frame_rate)`, computed
  in integers. For PCM, `frame_rate` is the sample rate and `hop` is the hop in samples; for
  scores, they are the detector's rate and hop. The last frame ends at the audio length.
- Durations in configurations are converted to whole frames or samples in integer arithmetic when
  used: the maximum piece length rounds down; segmentation durations and padding round to
  nearest.
- Cuts, segment boundaries and trim bounds fall on frame boundaries (10 ms by default), except
  that the last boundary is the audio length.

## Analysis (PCM)

- `AnalyzeConfig::default()`: 30 ms window, 10 ms hop. `frames(window, hop)` requires
  `0 < hop <= window`. The window is centered on its hop and clipped at the ends of the audio.
- Each channel is high-passed at 80 Hz (second-order Butterworth) for detection only. Channel
  powers are averaged; the frame value is `10 * log10(mean power)` in dBFS (full-scale sine = -3).
- A frame is digital zero when every raw sample of every channel in its window is zero. Its value
  is -200 dB, it is excluded from the level percentiles, and it starts as silence (the minimum
  silence rule still applies).
- Samples that are not finite (NaN, infinity) are read as zero.
- Push blocks may have any size; a partial interleaved frame is kept for the next push and dropped
  by `finish`. `push_planar` panics if the slice count differs from the channel count, the slices
  differ in length, or a partial interleaved frame is pending.
- About 1.8 MB of frame data per hour at the default hop.
- `Analyzer::new` errors: `ZeroSampleRate`, `ZeroChannels`, `SampleRateTooLow` (<= 160 Hz),
  `HopTooShort` (hop rounds to 0 samples), `InvalidFrames` (hop over `u32::MAX` samples).

## External scores

- `from_scores(layout, len, score_rate, hop, scores)`: `len` is the original length in samples per
  channel; `hop` is in samples at `score_rate`; scores are speech probabilities in `0.0..=1.0`.
- Each frame must span at least one original sample (`hop * sample_rate >= score_rate`), else
  `InvalidScoreFrames` (also for a zero rate or hop).
- The scores must cover the audio: the last score starts before `len`, and less than one hop may
  be missing at the end. Otherwise `FrameCountMismatch`. Other errors: `InvalidValue` (score
  outside `0.0..=1.0` or NaN), `ZeroSampleRate`, `ZeroChannels`.

## Segmentation

- `SegmentConfig::default()`: `Threshold::Auto`, minimum silence 250 ms, minimum sound 100 ms,
  padding 100 ms before sound (`pre`) and 200 ms after (`tail`). Setters: `threshold(t)?`,
  `min_silence(d)`, `min_sound(d)`, `padding(pre, tail)`.
- Levels: `floor` and `ref` are the 10th and 99th percentile of non-digital-zero frame values.
- `Threshold::Auto`: PCM sound starts at `on = max(floor + 4, min(floor + 6, ref - 20))` dB and
  ends below `on - 3`; scores start at 0.5 and end below 0.35. `Abs(v)`: `on = off = v`.
  `BelowRef(d)`: `on = off = ref - d`. Only `Auto` has hysteresis. `threshold` errors with
  `InvalidThreshold` for non-finite values or a negative `BelowRef`.
- A silent frame becomes sound at `value >= on` and sound stays sound while `value >= off`. Sound
  runs shorter than the minimum sound become silence, then silence runs shorter than the minimum
  silence become sound, also at either end of the audio.
- `segments` returns spans covering `[0, len)` in order. Sound spans include padding; when the
  paddings of two sounds overlap, the overlap is split in its middle (kept inside the silence) and
  the two sound spans are adjacent. `trim` returns the first padded sound start to the last padded
  sound end, or `None` if there is no sound.

## Planning

- `PlanConfig::new(min, target, max)?` requires `min <= target <= max` and `target > 0`
  (`InvalidLengths`). `max` is hard and includes padding; `min` is soft (penalized, flagged).
- Setters: `count(NonZeroUsize)` (exact piece count, target becomes span / count; fewer pieces only
  when the frame boundaries outside dropped ranges cannot support the count),
  `gap(Gap::Keep | Gap::Drop)` (default `Keep`),
  `placement(Placement::Quietest | Center | Ratio(r))?` (default `Quietest`, `InvalidRatio`
  outside `0.0..=1.0`), `weights(Weights)?` (`InvalidWeights`).
- `Weights` (non-exhaustive; build with `Weights::default()` and assign fields): `cut` 0.1 (must be
  > 0), `level` 1, `pause` 1, `pause_ref` 500 ms (non-zero), `target` 1, `short` 4.
- Cut cost: `cut + level * norm + pause * (1 - min(1, q / pause_ref))`. `norm` is the level
  smoothed over 150 ms, scaled to `0..=1` between `floor` and `max(ref, floor + 20 dB)` (scores are
  used as is). `q` is the length of the below-`off` stretch at the cut; for a silence candidate,
  the silence length. Piece cost: `target * ((len - target_len) / target_len)^2`, plus
  `short * (min - len) / min` below the minimum.
- Grid block: `min(1 s, max((max - min) / 2, max / 8))`, at least one frame. Padding longer than
  the maximum less two blocks is shortened to that for planning.
- Candidates: one per interior silence, and the quietest point of each grid block outside
  silences; blocks restart after each silence. With `Gap::Keep`, a silence longer than `max` minus
  two blocks also gets grid candidates between its padding (reason `Silence`). Leading and trailing
  silence never get a silence candidate.
- If adjacent candidates are farther apart than `max`, additional frame boundaries bridge them,
  including within padding. No point is inserted inside a dropped range.
- Silence candidate: within `[start + tail, end - pre]` when non-empty. `Keep` cuts at one point
  chosen by `placement`; `Drop` drops that whole range. When the silence is shorter than
  `pre + tail`, both cut at the middle of the padding overlap.
- `Drop` also drops leading silence up to `pre` before the first sound and trailing silence after
  `tail` past the last sound. An all-silent input gives an empty plan with `Drop`.
- The dynamic program minimizes the total cost with every piece within `max`. A single frame
  longer than `max` cannot be split and is flagged. Ties keep the earlier predecessor. Deterministic.
- Count mode first tries the acoustic candidates under the requested maximum. If they cannot meet
  both limits, a reachability pass over the implicit full frame grid, accounting for removable
  silence ranges, supplies a feasible path. Equal shares of the retained frame grid supply enough
  positions for the exact count. Only if the full grid cannot meet `max` is the planning limit
  raised, by binary search, to the smallest attainable longest piece. Pieces are still flagged
  against the requested maximum; fewer pieces are returned only if the available frame boundaries
  outside dropped ranges cannot support the requested count.
- Reasons: `Silence` for silence candidates and grid points inside a silence, `Quiet` for other grid
  points with `norm <= 0.25`, `Forced` otherwise.
- `Plan { pieces, cuts }`: `cuts[i]` separates `pieces[i]` and `pieces[i + 1]`;
  `pieces[i].end == cuts[i].end`, `pieces[i + 1].start == cuts[i].start`. With `Keep`,
  `cut.end == cut.start` and pieces cover `[0, len)`. `Piece` flags: `too_short` (below `min`),
  `too_long` (above `max`). Empty audio gives an empty plan.
- Count mode takes `O(count * candidates * candidates within max)` time and 4 bytes per count and
  candidate.

## Adjust

- `adjust(analysis, segment, points, window)` keeps all audio. Points are sorted and deduplicated;
  points `<= 0` or `>= len` are ignored.
- Candidates are the silence candidates, the quietest point of each block of `min(1 s, window)`
  outside silences, and within every silence (clear of its padding) grid points with reason
  `Silence`.
- Each point `p` picks, among candidates within `window` of it and before the midpoints to its
  neighbours, the lowest `cut cost + |x - p| / window` with default weights and
  `Placement::Quietest`.
- A point without candidates becomes a `Forced` cut at the nearest frame boundary. Cuts at the
  same boundary as the previous one or at either end are skipped. Piece flags are always false.

## Features

- `std` (default), `libm` (required without `std`; the crate is `no_std` + `alloc`), `serde`
  (`Serialize`/`Deserialize` for `Analysis`, `Layout`, `Plan`, `Piece`, `Cut`, `CutReason`, `Span`,
  `Kind`; deserializing `Analysis` validates it and fails with the matching `ConfigError`
  message).

## Non-goals

Voice activity models, decoding/encoding, resampling, loudness measurement, quality checks, breath
detection, editing-program formats and CSV, music editing, speech recognition.
